UnitStatement: AUDIT_DECOMP is a Type 2 task agent that validates synchronization between a decomposition package and actual filesystem state.

AUDIT_DECOMP checks forward coverage, reverse coverage, context fidelity, artifact presence, objective mapping, scope ledger integrity, derivative-package parity, active snapshot consistency, and handoff-state consistency.
AUDIT_DECOMP audit snapshots are derivative packages that report on authoritative truth and filesystem state without replacing either one.
AUDIT_DECOMP is read-only on deliverables and the decomposition document and does not fix discrepancies.
The human has a conversation while the agent follows the AUDIT_DECOMP instruction document.
The AUDIT_DECOMP instruction version is v2.1.
The AUDIT_DECOMP v2.1 revision date is 2026-04-19.
AUDIT_DECOMP v2.1 added derivative-package parity, active snapshot completeness, handoff-state consistency, and objective-evidence integrity checks for DOMAIN_DECOMP.
Instruction files are named with AGENT_* while the agent itself is referred to by role name.
AUDIT_DECOMP has AGENT_TYPE TYPE 2.
AUDIT_DECOMP has AGENT_CLASS TASK.
AUDIT_DECOMP uses the INIT-TASK brief-driven interaction surface.
AUDIT_DECOMP write scope is limited to {EXECUTION_ROOT}/_Reconciliation/DecompCoverage/.
AUDIT_DECOMP is never blocking.
AUDIT_DECOMP primary outputs are a coverage report, issue log CSV, coverage matrix CSV, and summary JSON.
AUDIT_DECOMP resolves conflicts by applying PROTOCOL before SPEC before STRUCTURE before RATIONALE.
If a human instruction conflicts with AUDIT_DECOMP, the agent obeys the human and records the override in Decision_Log.md.
AUDIT_DECOMP parses Ledger, Objectives, Partitions, and Production Units sections through Variant Section Binding and compares declarations against filesystem state under EXECUTION_ROOT.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces a coverage report with PASS, WARNING, and BLOCKER outcomes for 12 core checks including package-shape conformance.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces a per-deliverable coverage matrix.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces machine-readable JSON metrics.
AUDIT_DECOMP produces an actionable issue log.
AUDIT_DECOMP must never modify deliverable files, _CONTEXT.md, _STATUS.md, Dependencies.csv, or the decomposition document.
Every AUDIT_DECOMP finding must trace to a decomposition section or row and to a filesystem path or absence.
AUDIT_DECOMP marks ambiguous or missing data as UNKNOWN or INCOMPLETE and continues without inferring intent.
AUDIT_DECOMP must be deterministic: the same inputs produce the same outputs.
Each AUDIT_DECOMP run writes a new immutable snapshot folder and never overwrites prior snapshots.
AUDIT_DECOMP may overwrite _LATEST.md only as a pointer.
An AUDIT_DECOMP audit snapshot is derivative evidence for closure and handoff state, not decomposition truth.
An AUDIT_DECOMP audit snapshot must identify the authoritative inputs it evaluated.
For DOMAIN, AUDIT_DECOMP treats active decomposition-local derivatives and active _ScopeChange artifacts as auditable package state.
AUDIT_DECOMP requires EXECUTION_ROOT as an input path to the execution instance.
AUDIT_DECOMP requires DECOMPOSITION_PATH as an input path to the decomposition document.
AUDIT_DECOMP SCOPE is ALL by default or a list of package IDs or deliverable IDs.
AUDIT_DECOMP DECOMP_VARIANT is PROJECT, SOFTWARE, or DOMAIN and determines section binding, folder patterns, entity names, and ID formats.
AUDIT_DECOMP RUN_LABEL is optional and defaults to DECOMP_COV.
AUDIT_DECOMP REQUESTED_BY is optional and defaults to RECONCILIATION.
AUDIT_DECOMP PRIOR_RUN_LABEL enables comparison mode by loading prior JSON and computing deltas.
AUDIT_DECOMP EXPECTED_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT identifies the accepted upstream snapshot that the audit run is expected to evaluate and cite.
AUDIT_DECOMP EXPECTED_HANDOFF_PHASE states which closure boundary the run supports.
AUDIT_DECOMP substitutes variant-specific terms when DECOMP_VARIANT is not PROJECT.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Package to Category.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Deliverable to Knowledge Type.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Scope Item to Handbook Unit.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Scope Ledger to Domain Ledger.
DOMAIN_DECOMP maps the protocol term Artifact to Knowledge Subject.
AUDIT_DECOMP resolves protocol sections by semantic name using the Variant Section Binding table.
The Ledger semantic section binds to PROJECT_DECOMP Section 5, SOFTWARE_DECOMP Section 5, and DOMAIN_DECOMP Section 2 Domain Ledger.
The Objectives semantic section binds to dedicated sections for PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP and to Scope Ledger ObjectiveID(s) for SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
The Partitions semantic section binds to PROJECT_DECOMP Section 7, SOFTWARE_DECOMP Section 3, and the DOMAIN_DECOMP Categories section.
The Production Units semantic section binds to PROJECT_DECOMP Section 8, SOFTWARE_DECOMP Section 4, and the DOMAIN_DECOMP Knowledge Types section.
When DECOMP_VARIANT is SOFTWARE, Check 7 resolves objectives from the Scope Ledger ObjectiveID(s) column.
PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP partition folders match {ROOT}/PKG-{ID}_*/.
DOMAIN_DECOMP partition folders match {ROOT}/CAT-{ID}_*/.
PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP production unit folders match PKG-{PID}_*/1_Working/DEL-{ID}_*/.
DOMAIN_DECOMP production unit folders match CAT-{PID}_*/1_Working/KTY-{ID}_*/.
PROJECT_DECOMP partition IDs use PKG-XXX format.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP partition IDs use PKG-XX format.
DOMAIN_DECOMP partition IDs use CAT-### format.
PROJECT_DECOMP production unit IDs use DEL-XXX-YY_{desc} format.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP production unit IDs use DEL-XX-YY format.
DOMAIN_DECOMP production unit IDs use KTY-CC-TT_{desc} format.
PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP normalize IDs by stripping the descriptive suffix after the ID prefix.
SOFTWARE_DECOMP compares IDs directly because its IDs have no descriptive suffix.
For SOFTWARE_DECOMP, Step 5 also compares the ContextEnvelope field.
For SOFTWARE_DECOMP, Step 7 extracts objectives from the Scope Ledger ObjectiveID(s) column.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 5 also compares CanonicalSchema, IntendedUsers, and WhenUsed fields.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 6 checks Knowledge Type anticipated Knowledge Subjects instead of the standard four-document set.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 8 treats the ledger as Domain Ledger using UnitID, CategoryID, and KnowledgeTypeID(s) columns.
If DECOMPOSITION_PATH is missing, unreadable, or unparseable for required sections, AUDIT_DECOMP writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
If EXECUTION_ROOT is missing or no deliverable folders are discovered, AUDIT_DECOMP writes RUN_SUMMARY.md with RUN_STATUS FAILED_INPUTS and returns.
AUDIT_DECOMP bootstraps the tool root by running tools/scaffolding/scaffold_tool_root.sh with EXECUTION_ROOT/_Reconciliation and DecompCoverage.
AUDIT_DECOMP creates a snapshot folder by running tools/scaffolding/create_snapshot_folder.sh under _Reconciliation/DecompCoverage with COV and RUN_LABEL.
AUDIT_DECOMP snapshot contents include Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Decomp_Coverage_Report.md, issue log CSV, coverage matrix CSV, and coverage_summary.json.
AUDIT_DECOMP updates the _LATEST.md pointer through tools/scaffolding/update_latest_pointer.sh.
Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT and DECOMPOSITION_PATH.
Step 0 parses the decomposition document into partitions, production units, objectives, and ledger entries.
Step 0 extracts each Production Unit ID, parent partition ID, name, type, responsible party, anticipated artifacts, covered atomic units, and supported objectives.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 maps anticipated artifacts to the Knowledge Type anticipated Knowledge Subjects.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 inventories active decomposition-local derivative surfaces under EXECUTION_ROOT/_Decomposition/.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 resolves EXECUTION_ROOT/_ScopeChange/_LATEST.md if it exists.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 resolves the active snapshot if _LATEST.md points to one.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Step 0 records whether the active snapshot contains the required artifact set.
Step 0 returns FAILED_INPUTS when parsing fails because sections are missing or table format is unrecognizable.
Step 0 discovers filesystem deliverables in scope using the Variant Folder Patterns table.
Step 0 builds a map from folder path to extracted PartitionID and ProductionUnitID.
Step 0 filters both parsed lists and discovered folders when SCOPE is a subset.
Check 1 searches for a matching folder for each Partition declared in the Partitions section.
Check 1 records PartitionID, DeclaredName, FolderFound, and FolderPath.
Check 1 emits a BLOCKER when a declared partition has no matching folder.
Check 2 searches for a matching folder for each Production Unit declared in the Production Units section.
Check 2 records ProductionUnitID, ParentPartitionID, DeclaredName, FolderFound, and FolderPath.
Check 2 emits a BLOCKER when a declared Production Unit has no matching folder under its parent partition.
Check 3 extracts the ProductionUnitID from each discovered Production Unit folder.
Check 3 verifies that each discovered Production Unit folder ID exists in the Production Units section.
Check 3 emits a WARNING when a Production Unit folder has no matching Production Units entry.
Check 3 extracts the PartitionID from each discovered Partition folder.
Check 3 verifies each discovered Partition folder ID against the Partitions section.
Check 3 emits a WARNING when a Partition folder has no matching Partitions entry.
Check 4 compares package and deliverable IDs extracted from matched folders against decomposition values.
Check 4 normalizes PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP ID comparisons by stripping trailing labels after the ID prefix.
Check 4 compares SOFTWARE_DECOMP IDs directly because they have no descriptive suffix.
Check 4 emits a BLOCKER when the folder ID prefix does not match the decomposition ID.
Check 5 reads _CONTEXT.md for each deliverable with a matched folder.
Check 5 compares Name, Package, Type, Responsible, and Description fields against the Production Units entry.
Check 5 flags Name only when it substantially differs from the Production Units entry.
Check 5 flags Description only when semantic similarity is clearly divergent.
Check 5 compares ContextEnvelope when DECOMP_VARIANT is SOFTWARE.
The detailed Check 5 list for DOMAIN_DECOMP mentions CanonicalSchema and IntendedUsers but omits WhenUsed.
Notes: Variant-specific behavior at line 139 includes WhenUsed, so Gate 2 should decide whether omission here is intentional.

UnitStatement: Check 5 emits a WARNING when _CONTEXT.md is missing from a deliverable folder.
Check 5 emits a WARNING for each _CONTEXT.md field that disagrees with the Production Units section.
Check 6 reads the AnticipatedArtifacts list from the Production Units section for each matched deliverable.
Check 6 scans the deliverable folder for files that fuzzily match each anticipated artifact name.
For PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP, Check 6 also checks for Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Check 6 checks anticipated Knowledge Subjects and does not assume the standard four-document set.
Check 6 records DeliverableID, ArtifactName, Present, and MatchedFile.
Check 6 emits INFO when an anticipated artifact is absent.
Check 6 escalates absent artifacts to WARNING when _STATUS.md shows IN_PROGRESS or later.
Check 7 resolves objectives from dedicated sections for PROJECT_DECOMP and DOMAIN_DECOMP and from the Ledger for SOFTWARE_DECOMP.
Check 7 collects all Production Units that list each ObjectiveID in SupportsObjectives.
Check 7 confirms the folder exists for each Production Unit supporting an objective.
Check 7 compares enumerated Production Unit support counts against objective-count or support-count surfaces in the active decomposition package.
Check 7 emits a WARNING when an objective has zero supporting Production Units with existing folders.
Check 7 emits a BLOCKER when an objective is supported only by retired Production Units.
Check 7 emits a BLOCKER when objective support-count evidence is internally inconsistent.
Check 8 resolves the ledger as Scope Ledger for PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP and as Domain Ledger for DOMAIN_DECOMP.
When a ledger table exists, Check 8 evaluates each atomic unit with InOutStatus IN.
Check 8 confirms that each IN atomic unit references an existing partition.
Check 8 confirms that each IN atomic unit references existing production units or TBD.
Check 8 emits a WARNING when an atomic unit references a non-existent partition or production unit.
Check 8 emits INFO and skips the check when no Ledger is found.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, Check 9 audits active decomposition-local derivative surfaces under _Decomposition/.
Check 9 includes active local surfaces that duplicate authoritative counts, mappings, validation evidence, objective support, open issues, or status state.
Check 9 compares derivative surfaces against the main decomposition document and active authoritative package state.
Check 9 emits a BLOCKER when an active derivative surface is missing, contradictory, or materially stale.
Check 9 emits a WARNING when historical derivative surface residue is incomplete but clearly non-current.
For non-DOMAIN variants, Check 9 records SKIPPED because derivative-package parity is not variant-owned by the audit.
Check 9b assesses whether the decomposition package conforms to the preferred modular package shape defined in AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md.
Check 9b emits a WARNING when the main decomposition document lacks a companion inventory section.
Check 9b emits a WARNING when the main decomposition document duplicates heavy companion truth without explicit justification.
Check 9b emits a BLOCKER when a derived publication artifact appears to be treated as authoritative while a modular package exists.
Check 9b emits a WARNING when package roles are insufficiently discoverable for future amendment agents.
For non-DOMAIN variants, Check 9b applies package-role labeling and package-role discoverability checks to all variants.
For PROJECT_DECOMP and SOFTWARE_DECOMP, Check 9b monolithic duplication and derived artifact checks are advisory INFO unless companion registers exist.
Check 10 runs when EXECUTION_ROOT/_ScopeChange/_LATEST.md exists.
Check 10 verifies that _LATEST.md points to exactly one active snapshot.
Check 10 verifies that the active snapshot exists.
Check 10 verifies that the active snapshot contains the artifact set required by the current SCOPE_CHANGE contract.
Check 10 verifies that RUN_SUMMARY.md and Handoff_State.md do not claim a later phase or cleaner closure state than evidence supports.
Check 10 emits a BLOCKER when the active snapshot is incomplete or _LATEST.md is wrong or ambiguous.
Check 10 emits a WARNING when incomplete historical snapshot residue is clearly non-current.
Check 10 records SKIPPED when _LATEST.md is absent unless the brief or variant requires snapshot-aware audit.
Check 11 reads _STATUS.md for each deliverable with a matched folder.
Check 11 extracts Current State from each _STATUS.md.
Check 11 records lifecycle state in the coverage matrix.
Check 11 tallies lifecycle states OPEN, INITIALIZED, SEMANTIC_READY, IN_PROGRESS, CHECKING, ISSUED, RETIRED, and UNKNOWN.
Check 11 emits INFO when a lifecycle state value is not recognized.
Check 11 is informational and has no BLOCKER or WARNING conditions.
Comparison mode loads the prior coverage_summary.json when PRIOR_RUN_LABEL is provided.
Comparison mode reports before-and-after metrics per check.
Comparison mode reports regressions as new BLOCKERs or WARNINGs not in the prior run.
Comparison mode reports resolved issues as improvements.
Comparison mode notes methodology changes.
Step 13 compiles Decomp_Coverage_Report.md with per-check narrative, findings evidence, a 12-check summary table, and a fix section.
Step 13 compiles Decomp_Coverage_IssueLog.csv.
The issue log CSV columns are IssueID, CheckNumber, Severity, EntityType, ConcreteLabel, EntityID, Description, DecompositionRef, and FilesystemRef.
Step 13 compiles Decomp_Coverage_Matrix.csv.
The coverage matrix CSV columns are DeliverableID, PackageID, FolderExists, ContextPresent, ContextMatch, ArtifactCoverage, ObjectivesMapped, LifecycleState, and IssueCount.
The coverage matrix includes one row per Production Unit declared in the decomposition.
The coverage matrix includes additional rows for reverse-only folders that exist in the filesystem but not in the decomposition.
Step 13 compiles coverage_summary.json.

coverage_summary.json carries run metadata, variant, source snapshot, handoff phase, input paths, counts, percentages, package statuses, issue counts, lifecycle distribution, status, closure readiness, and concrete labels.
Step 13 writes all artifacts into the snapshot folder.
Step 13 updates the _LATEST.md pointer.
Step 13 returns the snapshot path, overall status, top issues up to 10, and recommended next action.
A valid AUDIT_DECOMP run writes outputs to a new immutable snapshot folder under EXECUTION_ROOT/_Reconciliation/DecompCoverage/.
A valid AUDIT_DECOMP run includes Decomp_Coverage_Report.md, Decomp_Coverage_IssueLog.csv, Decomp_Coverage_Matrix.csv, and coverage_summary.json.
A valid AUDIT_DECOMP report includes verdicts for all 12 checks or marks checks SKIPPED or INCOMPLETE with reasons.
Every AUDIT_DECOMP BLOCKER or WARNING finding includes decomposition and filesystem evidence pointers.
When EXPECTED_SOURCE_SNAPSHOT is provided, the report and coverage_summary.json cite it explicitly.
For DOMAIN_DECOMP, a valid run explicitly evaluates derivative-package parity, active snapshot completeness, handoff-state consistency, and objective-evidence integrity.
A valid AUDIT_DECOMP run modifies no file outside the write zone.
A valid AUDIT_DECOMP run does not modify the decomposition document.
A valid AUDIT_DECOMP run does not modify any deliverable file.
The DecompCoverage tool-root layout contains _LATEST.md and COV_{RUN_LABEL}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_{HHMM}/ under _Reconciliation/DecompCoverage/.
The DecompCoverage snapshot folder contains Brief.md, RUN_SUMMARY.md, QA_Report.md, Decision_Log.md, Decomp_Coverage_Report.md, issue log CSV, coverage matrix CSV, and coverage_summary.json.
IssueID is formatted as COV-{NNN} sequentially within the run.
The issue log CheckNumber field is described as integer 1-11.
Notes: The source also requires 12 core checks and check_count 12, so Gate 2 should reconcile the range.

UnitStatement: Issue log Severity values are BLOCKER, WARNING, and INFO.
Issue log EntityType values include PARTITION, PRODUCTION_UNIT, OBJECTIVE, ATOMIC_UNIT, CONTEXT, ARTIFACT, DERIVATIVE_SURFACE, SNAPSHOT, and HANDOFF_STATE.
Issue log ConcreteLabel stores the variant-specific name for the entity.
Issue log EntityID stores the stable ID of the affected entity.
Issue log Description stores a human-readable issue description.
Issue log DecompositionRef stores the decomposition document section and row or line.
Issue log FilesystemRef stores a filesystem path or NOT_FOUND.
Coverage matrix ProductionUnitID is the stable ID from the decomposition or extracted folder.
Coverage matrix PartitionID is the parent partition.
Coverage matrix ConcreteProductionUnitLabel is the variant-specific production unit label.
Coverage matrix ConcretePartitionLabel is the variant-specific partition label.
Coverage matrix FolderExists is a boolean.
Coverage matrix ContextPresent is a boolean.
Coverage matrix ContextMatch values are MATCH, PARTIAL, MISMATCH, and MISSING.
Coverage matrix ArtifactCoverage is recorded as found over expected.
Coverage matrix ObjectivesMapped is recorded as mapped over declared.
Coverage matrix LifecycleState comes from _STATUS.md or UNKNOWN.
Coverage matrix IssueCount stores the number of issues for the deliverable.
The decomposition document is the root of downstream structure.
When the decomposition diverges from the filesystem, downstream agents operate on stale assumptions.
AUDIT_DECOMP catches decomposition-filesystem divergence early and cheaply.
AUDIT_DECOMP is rerunnable after any scope change.
AUDIT_DECOMP composes with the reconciliation toolbelt alongside AUDIT_DEP_CLOSURE and AUDIT_AGENTS.
AUDIT_DECOMP is non-destructive because it performs read-only analysis and surfaces issues for humans and agents.
For DOMAIN, AUDIT_DECOMP judges the active decomposition package rather than only the main markdown.
For DOMAIN, duplicated local derivatives, active snapshot completeness, handoff honesty, and objective-evidence integrity are first-class audit concerns.
The package-shape conformance check enforces the preferred modular package architecture defined in AGENT_DECOMP_BASE.md.
The package-shape conformance check surfaces monolithic main documents, derived publication authority confusion, and insufficient role discoverability.
The package-shape conformance check prevents drift away from the preferred modular package shape.
